note: Briefs b01-b12 were the pilot's; b13-b36 complete the full study's design (protocol, Novel briefs): three in each of twelve strata of register, density and whether a chart is required. Written without reference to examples/, so no arm can succeed by imitating a page it was shown. Each is given to the model alone; the file is never passed whole.

briefs.brief: A single page announcing that a small research lab is opening its measurement toolkit to the public. It should feel like a statement of intent, not a product page. One headline, a short argument in three or four paragraphs, and a way to get the toolkit.
A page for a one-day conference on instrumentation and craft. Name, date, city, a paragraph on why it exists, the six talks with speaker names, and a registration call to action.

A point-of-view page arguing that most organisations measure the wrong things. Long-form and opinionated, with a strong opening claim, three supporting sections, and a closing position. Written to be read, not skimmed.

A hiring page for a four-person team that builds internal tooling. What the team does, how it works, the two open roles with responsibilities, and how to apply. Should read as though a person wrote it.
A page marking the tenth release of a long-running open-source library. A retrospective note, the three changes that mattered most, thanks to contributors, and where to read the changelog.

A public transparency page for a small company: how many customers it serves, uptime over the last year, and how it spends revenue. One chart of uptime by month, one of spend by category, and honest commentary on both.

An incident postmortem for a four-hour outage of a payments service. Summary, timeline with timestamps, root cause, customer impact, what went well, what did not, and dated remediation items with owners.

A quarterly operating review for an internal audience. Headline metrics, a chart of monthly active accounts across the quarter, a chart of support ticket volume by category, a table of the top five accounts by usage, and terse analytical commentary.
A pricing and plan comparison for a developer tool with three tiers. A comparison table covering at least ten capabilities, the limits of each tier, notes on overage billing, and a short FAQ.

A reference page documenting the fields of an event payload: field name, type, whether required, default, and description, for about eighteen fields, grouped into three sections, with a worked example payload.

A settings page for a notification system: grouped preference controls with labels and explanatory text, toggles and radio choices, a destructive action, and a save control. Interactive form controls throughout.

A summary of an A/B experiment that did not reach significance. The hypothesis, the design, a chart of the two arms over time, the observed effect with its confidence interval, and a recommendation not to ship.
A single page marking a city library's first year of free evening opening. One headline, a sentence on why it was done, one chart of evening visits by month, and a closing line inviting people in.

A page from a small charity announcing that it has met its clean-water target. The figure stated plainly, one chart of wells completed by year since founding, a short thank-you to donors, and a link to the full report.

A launch page for a bicycle courier co-operative's annual impact statement. A statement of what the co-operative is for, one chart of deliveries made by bike rather than van over five years, and how to become a member.

A page introducing a family-run ceramics studio and its approach to making. The studio's story in a few paragraphs, the three ranges it makes with a short description of each, a note on commissions, and how to visit the workshop.

A public page from a regional rail operator explaining why trains were late last winter. An honest opening, the three main causes, one chart of punctuality by week through the winter, what is changing, and how passengers can claim compensation.

An essay page from a design school arguing that students should learn to read data before they learn to style it. A strong opening claim, two supporting sections, one chart of how graduates' first roles have shifted over a decade, and a closing position.

A long-form annual letter from the founder of a mid-sized engineering firm. Opening reflections, sections on the year's projects, people, mistakes made and what was learned, plans for next year, and a signed close. Substantial and meant to be read in full.

A guide page for a museum's temporary exhibition on the history of timekeeping. An introduction, eight rooms each with a title and a paragraph, highlights to look out for, accessibility information, opening hours, and ticket prices.

A manifesto page for a network of community energy groups. A preamble, ten numbered principles each with a short explanation, how groups join, the governance model in brief, and a list of founding members by region.

A public annual review from a national park authority. A foreword, sections on conservation, visitors, volunteers and finances, a chart of visitor numbers by season over three years, a chart of income by source, and a forward look.

A long-form story page from a newspaper on how a river was brought back from pollution. An opening scene, several sections tracing the decades, quotes from people involved, a chart of water quality readings over thirty years, and a closing reflection.

A climate report page from a mid-sized retailer. An opening commitment, sections on emissions, suppliers, packaging and transport, a chart of emissions by scope over four years, a chart of packaging weight per order, and the targets for the next five years.
A sign-in page for a team workspace product: email and password fields, a remember-me option, a link to reset a password, a single-sign-on option, and a short notice about scheduled maintenance.

An empty state for a project management tool when a user has no projects yet. A short explanation, one primary action to create a project, a secondary action to import from a spreadsheet, and a link to a guide.

A confirmation page shown after a customer cancels a subscription. What happens to their data and when, the date access ends, a way to undo the cancellation, and an optional single-question feedback field.
A status page for a hosted database service. The current state of each of four regions, one chart of response latency over the last twenty-four hours, and a short note on the most recent incident.
A personal usage page in a cloud storage product. Storage used against the plan limit, one chart of storage growth over the past six months, and a single action to upgrade the plan.

A single metric detail view in an analytics tool: the metric's name and definition, its current value against last period, one chart of the metric by day for ninety days, and a control to change the date range.

An account billing page for a software subscription: current plan, next invoice date and amount, a payment method on file with an option to change it, a list of the last six invoices with download links, and a cancel action.

A team member management page: a list of members with name, email, role and last active date, a way to invite someone by email with a role choice, role descriptions, and an action to remove a member that asks for confirmation.

A weekly digest page in an internal sales tool. Four headline figures with change against last week, one chart of pipeline value by stage, a list of the five largest deals that moved, and a short note from the sales lead.

A model evaluation summary for a machine learning team. The model and dataset, a table of five metrics against the previous version, one chart of accuracy by class, known failure cases in a short list, and a recommendation on release.

An operations dashboard for a warehouse. Today's orders received, picked, packed and shipped, a chart of throughput by hour, a chart of pick errors by aisle, a table of delayed orders with reasons, and staffing by shift.

A clinical trial site monitoring page for a research coordinator. Enrolment against target, a chart of enrolment by month for each of six sites, a table of protocol deviations with severity and status, upcoming visit windows, and data query counts by site.
